picks.why: JPM is the most direct way to hold my bank-margin call: it is the largest XLF bank, it sits about 2% below its $359.30 52-week high, the yield curve is +45 bp and steepening, and the Basel III re-proposal lowers capital requirements for large banks.

Schwab's bank earns more as the curve steepens while the Fed holds short rates, and it has the steadiest uptrend of the eligible financials: +3.2% on the week, +8.5% over 4 weeks and +18.8% over 12 weeks.

Mastercard rose 6.2% last week after reporting and does not report again until Oct 29; it shares the XLF inflows but carries less credit and rate risk than the banks, which spreads Friday's jobs-report risk within my top sector.

KO is the book's hedge for Friday's jobs report: a Q2 beat (EPS $0.97 vs $0.93 expected) lifted it 6.5% to within 4% of its 52-week high, and as a multinational it gains from the weaker dollar and cheaper inputs my staples thesis relies on.
REGN is my low-correlation healthcare pick and the sector's strongest move, up 16.3% last week to 7% below its $821 all-time high; the sheet shows its next report on 2026-10-28, not this week.

summary: Financials is my strongest sector call, so it gets three picks: JPM for the Basel III and curve thesis, SCHW because its bank gains from the steeper curve, and MA for post-earnings momentum with less credit and rate risk. KO and REGN do not move closely with the market and hedge a weak jobs report on Friday. I left out Communication Services (its eligible names are broken or one stock's momentum run) and passed on BTC and GLD, which are down 22% and 14% over 12 weeks with the 10-year yield at a 52-week high.
